_note: Curated seed of well-known CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities. Descriptions are summaries; verify details against NVD and the official CISA KEV catalog, and refresh with scripts/import_intel.py.

items.name: Apache Log4j2 remote code execution (Log4Shell)
items.description: JNDI lookup injection in Apache Log4j2 lets an unauthenticated attacker who controls a logged string load and execute remote code.
items.action: Upgrade Log4j2 to a fixed release, remove the JndiLookup class where upgrade is impossible, and hunt for ${jndi: strings in logs.

items.name: Microsoft Netlogon elevation of privilege (Zerologon)
items.description: A cryptographic flaw in the Netlogon Remote Protocol allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a domain controller to take over the domain.
items.action: Apply the Microsoft Netlogon updates on all domain controllers and enforce secure RPC.

items.name: Windows Print Spooler remote code execution (PrintNightmare)
items.description: The Windows Print Spooler service improperly performs privileged file operations, enabling remote code execution as SYSTEM.
items.action: Apply Microsoft updates and disable the Print Spooler service on domain controllers and servers that do not print.

items.name: Progress MOVEit Transfer SQL injection
items.description: SQL injection in the MOVEit Transfer web application allows unauthenticated attackers to access the database and deploy web shells; it was mass-exploited for data theft.
items.action: Apply vendor patches, review for the LEMURLOOT web shell indicators and audit downloaded files.

items.name: Microsoft Exchange Server SSRF (ProxyLogon)
items.description: Server-side request forgery in on-premises Exchange allows attackers to authenticate as the Exchange server and chain further flaws to code execution.
items.action: Patch Exchange, run Microsoft's IOC scanning guidance and check for web shells in Exchange directories.

items.name: Microsoft Outlook elevation of privilege (NTLM leak)
items.description: A crafted calendar reminder causes Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled SMB server and leak the user's NTLM hash without user interaction.
items.action: Apply Outlook updates, block outbound SMB (TCP 445) at the perimeter and add sensitive users to Protected Users.

items.name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect command injection
items.description: Command injection in the GlobalProtect feature of certain PAN-OS versions allows unauthenticated root code execution on the firewall.
items.action: Upgrade to a fixed PAN-OS hotfix and follow vendor guidance on compromise assessment.

items.name: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway information disclosure (Citrix Bleed)
items.description: A buffer over-read leaks session tokens from NetScaler appliances, letting attackers hijack authenticated sessions and bypass MFA.
items.action: Patch NetScaler appliances and terminate all active and persistent sessions after patching.

items.name: Microsoft SMBv1 remote code execution (EternalBlue)
items.description: A flaw in the SMBv1 server allows remote code execution; it was used by WannaCry and NotPetya to spread laterally.
items.action: Apply MS17-010, disable SMBv1 and block SMB at network boundaries.
